question: Does the requested inheritance-based split preserve the Control UI chat-pane lifecycle closely enough to accept after an actual PR-head interaction run, or should the extraction be narrowed before merge?
rationale: The branch is a large, protected maintainer-requested refactor; tests establish useful regression coverage, but repository policy requires human acceptance of the structural boundary and the external proof gate still needs live behavior evidence.

options.title: Review with live proof
options.body: Require a redacted PR-head Control UI run covering startup, session switching, and a representative chat action, then complete the source-boundary review before landing.

options.title: Narrow the split
options.body: Keep the public entrypoint and extract fewer lifecycle layers if maintainers prefer lower inheritance and review complexity.

recommendation.title: Review with live proof
recommendation.body: Require a redacted PR-head Control UI run covering startup, session switching, and a representative chat action, then complete the source-boundary review before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns a key session-state contract that this refactor must preserve.
